# unifi_setting_usg_geo (Resource)

The `unifi_setting_usg_geo` resource manages Region Blocking (Geo IP filtering) for a UniFi gateway. On UniFi Network 10.x this is stored in a dedicated `usg_geo` setting (separate from `unifi_setting_usg`), with a nested `ip_filtering` object. Use it to block or allow traffic by country of origin.

This resource replaces the deprecated `geo_ip_filtering` block on `unifi_setting_usg`, which mapped to fields that no longer exist on current controllers.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Region Blocking (Geo IP filtering) on UniFi Network 10.x.
# Blocks all traffic to/from the listed countries.
resource "unifi_setting_usg_geo" "example" {
  ip_filtering = {
    action            = "block"
    countries         = ["RU", "CN", "KP"]
    traffic_direction = "both"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `ip_filtering` (Attributes) Region Blocking configuration. Uses IP geolocation to block or allow traffic based on the country of origin. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--ip_filtering))

### Optional

- `site` (String) The name of the UniFi site where this resource should be applied. If not specified, the default site will be used.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The unique identifier of this resource.

<a id="nestedatt--ip_filtering"></a>
### Nested Schema for `ip_filtering`

Required:

- `countries` (List of String) List of two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes to block or allow (e.g. `["RU", "CN"]`). Must contain at least one country code.

Optional:

- `action` (String) Whether the listed `countries` are blocked or allowed. Valid values are `block` (default — block the listed countries, allow all others) or `allow` (allow only the listed countries, block all others).
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether Region Blocking is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
- `traffic_direction` (String) Which traffic direction the filter applies to. Valid values are `both` (default), `ingress` (incoming only), or `egress` (outgoing only).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Region Blocking is a site-wide singleton; import with the site and the setting id.
terraform import unifi_setting_usg_geo.example default:<id>
```
